title: Cross-View PSD Distillation for Viewpoint-Robust Remote Photoplethysmography

contributions.purpose: Make rPPG heart-rate estimation robust to non-frontal camera viewpoints.
contributions.mechanism: Asymmetric cross-view PSD distillation that transfers frequency-domain (power spectral density) knowledge from a reliable frontal view to side views during training, exploiting the view-invariance of the cardiac PSD.
contributions.evaluation: On the MCD-rPPG dataset, reduces side-view heart rate MAE from 5.24 to 3.99 bpm (24% improvement) and the frontal-to-side gap by 34%.
contributions.source_quote: We propose a cross-view PSD distillation framework that transfers frequency-domain knowledge from frontal to side views, leveraging the view-invariant nature of heart rate.

contributions.purpose: Show that asymmetric treatment of views via stop-gradient is essential to avoid corrupting the frontal branch.
contributions.mechanism: Comparison of symmetric PSD consistency (gradients through both branches) versus applying stop-gradient to the teacher (frontal) view.
contributions.evaluation: Symmetric approaches cause catastrophic frontal degradation (MAE 2.91 to 11.06 bpm), while the asymmetric method preserves frontal quality.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that asymmetric design with stop-gradient is critical—symmetric approaches cause catastrophic frontal degradation (MAE: 2.91 -> 11.06 bpm), while our asymmetric method preserves frontal quality.

contributions.purpose: Improve side-view accuracy while simultaneously improving, not trading off, frontal performance.
contributions.mechanism: Training with the asymmetric PSD distillation loss on synchronized multi-camera MCD-rPPG data.
contributions.evaluation: 24% side-view MAE improvement (5.24 to 3.99 bpm) with frontal MAE improving from 2.91 to 2.45 bpm, reducing the frontal-to-side gap by 34%.
contributions.source_quote: On the MCD-rPPG dataset, our method achieves 24% improvement in side-view MAE (5.24 -> 3.99 bpm) while simultaneously improving frontal performance (2.91 -> 2.45 bpm), reducing the frontal-to-side gap by 34%.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Inspired by recent findings on asymmetry in Siamese representation learning (Chen & He, 2020; Wang et al., 2022), we apply a stop-gradient operation to the teacher (frontal) view, ensuring that only the student (side) view receives gradients from the PSD loss.
However, these methods primarily focus on cross-dataset generalization rather than cross-viewpoint robustness within the same recording session.
